title: Paula: Name Meaning, Origin & Personality
summary: Paula is a timeless and graceful name with deep historical roots across Europe and the Americas. It offers a wonderful blend of classic charm and gentle strength for a little girl.
origin: The name Paula has ancient Latin origins, derived from the Roman family name Paulus, which translates to small or humble. It functioned historically as the feminine form of Paul. The name spread widely throughout the Christian world due to Saint Paula, a prominent historical figure of the early church known for her scholarship and charity. Today, Paula remains a beloved and enduring choice across Europe, particularly in Spain, Germany, Scandinavia, and Latin America, appreciated for its traditional elegance and cross-cultural appeal.
personality: People often associate the name Paula with warmth, intelligence, and a grounded nature. Those with this name are frequently perceived as reliable friends, thoughtful listeners, and natural caregivers who bring a sense of calm to any room. There is an understated confidence to Paula, combining a gentle demeanor with a strong inner resolve. Others tend to view her as creative, intuitive, and deeply appreciative of beauty, art, and genuine human connections. This harmonious blend of empathy and steadfastness makes her a comforting and inspiring presence to those around her.
popularity: Paula is a classic name that enjoys steady, enduring popularity rather than fleeting trendiness. It is especially well-liked in Spanish-, Portuguese-, and German-speaking countries, where it frequently appears on birth registries across generations. While it may not currently sit at the absolute peak of naming charts in English-speaking regions, its familiar and sophisticated sound ensures it is always recognized and warmly received worldwide.

faq.q: Is Paula a popular name today?
faq.ans: Yes, Paula is considered a classic name that maintains steady popularity around the world, especially in Europe and Latin America. It is cherished for its timeless quality and lack of heavy generational attachment.

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Paula?
faq.ans: Paula originates from ancient Rome as the feminine form of the Latin family name Paulus. The root word relates to being small or humble.

faq.q: What are some common nicknames for Paula?
faq.ans: Popular nicknames for Paula include Polly, Pauli, Pau, and Lala. These affectionate short forms add a playful and modern touch to the traditional name.

faq.q: Does Paula have variations in other languages?
faq.ans: Yes, the name appears in many different cultures and languages with spellings like Paola in Italian, Paulette in French, and Pavlina in Slavic languages.
